A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PARL research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including proofs moved into Appendix B in v5.

before.justification: v4 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on MuJoCo, autonomous driving, and two interactive navigation tasks, including rewards, entropy estimates, trajectories, and learning curves.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds DDPG results on three existing MuJoCo tasks.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the surrogate entropy objective, PAPPO and PASAC updates, and model-learning procedure remain unchanged. The newly explicit rollout entropy formula documents evaluation rather than establishing a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Walker, Ant, HalfCheetah, Hopper, highway driving, roundabout driving, and the two Minigrid navigation tasks. DDPG is evaluated on existing tasks; partially observable environments are discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds DDPG for Ant, HalfCheetah, and Hopper alongside the retained RPC comparisons. The PPO and DQN comparisons elsewhere are unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 Appendix C.1 introduces a selection protocol for the new Ant DDPG baseline: train ten agents and select the best by mean reward. Retained experiments keep their stated settings; the explicit entropy-evaluation formula is newly documented, not evidence of a revised evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The trade-off parameter sweeps, deterministic versus stochastic policy evaluations, trajectory analyses, interactive navigation demonstrations, and learning curves are retained. Their relocation does not introduce new ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: v5 newly reports ten Ant DDPG training runs and selection of the best run. Existing five-agent SAC-based comparisons, ten-agent MuJoCo PPO/PAPPO evaluations, 50-episode evaluations, and uncertainty formats are retained. This does not establish increased runs for existing methods.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds DDPG reward and entropy-rate means: Ant 1371.23 and 4.14; HalfCheetah 10829.94 and 3.84; Hopper 1080.03 and 0.89, together with episode lengths and uncertainty values. All pre-existing numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 changes K(ε) from ε log(|X|−1)−ε log ε−(1−ε)log(1−ε) to ε log|X|−ε log ε and revises its proof. v5 also corrects the entropy chain-rule conditioning index and adds a two-state counterexample distinguishing stationary-distribution entropy from trajectory entropy. The principal theorem structure remains.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain entropy-rate minimization through a surrogate average reward, learned-model policy-gradient integration, and a reward–predictability trade-off. Replacing some references to predictable behaviour with predictable trajectories clarifies the existing focus rather than changing the contribution.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations of state predictability and the surrogate’s relationship to policy stochasticity, plus a substantive limitation concerning partially observable environments. It removes v4’s explicit explanation that the effects on deterministic MuJoCo tasks arise through imperfect learned models, while retaining a general discussion of deterministic environments.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly documents rollout entropy computation and states that it is applied equally across algorithms. v5 also supplies direct PARL repository links and redirects the hyperparameter reference from supplementary material to that repository. Existing model-training and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds Audenaert (2007), Berseth et al. (2021), and Mutti et al. (2021; 2022), including a comparison with SMiRL’s stationary-distribution objective. Moerland et al. and Watkins–Dayan references are removed. The Savas citation changes from preprint to publication metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: v5 adds explanatory paragraphs and footnotes, refines terminology, merges the problem statement into the entropy-estimation section, and moves the existing Lemma 1 and Proposition 1–2 proofs into a dedicated appendix. Most prose and the overall narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 are resized beside wrapping text; Figure 2 receives shorter labels and a clearer caption. Table 2 gains DDPG rows and an off-policy caption. Existing tables and appendix plots are redistributed, with no additional figures.

improvement.justification: The DDPG comparison, explicit entropy computation, repository links, and POMDP limitation improve documentation and assessment. However, the revised Proposition 1 proof switches from a bound involving 2T, with T defined as half the L1 distance, to K(ε) without reconciling that factor with the total-variation assumption. Removing the MuJoCo-specific model-error explanation also weakens interpretation. These gains and theoretical and explanatory weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
